page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, with support for AVX-512 and AES instructions. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n2-highmem-4 generally resides in the lower performance tiers for compute-heavy tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks fall into the bottom 25%, though the PassMark memory score registers in the middle 50% average. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average level, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench image processing drop to the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-4 trades raw computational speed for a dense memory allocation. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing, such as small-scale databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive text processing. However, the weak performance in compilation, ray tracing, and LLM inference indicates it is less suited for compute-intensive or graphics-heavy applications.
